title: The City Without a Moon
text:
Rain followed Sera and Rhen north for three days.

By the fourth morning the road was dry.

That was the first thing Sera disliked.

The second was the silence.

No carts. No birds. No arguments between merchants. Even the wind seemed unwilling to pass through the valley.

The city gate stood open.

A wooden sign identified the place as Yuecheng.

Sera stopped beneath it.

[[speaker:sera]]“You've heard of this place?”

Rhen looked up at the blank sky.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Once.”

[[speaker:sera]]“And?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“People used to say the moon was unusually beautiful here.”

Sera glanced upward.

It was noon.

[[speaker:sera]]“That's a strange thing to remember.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I remember strange things.”

She smiled.

[[speaker:sera]]“I noticed.”

They entered.

The first innkeeper they met was a woman named Ren Qiao, a city physician whose hands were stained permanently with herbal ink. She introduced herself while explaining that nobody in Yuecheng slept well anymore.

Sera asked why.

Ren looked genuinely confused.

[[speaker:ren]]“Why would they?”

Then she pointed toward the sky.

[[speaker:ren]]“There has not been a moon here for years.”

Sera stared.

Rhen did not.

That was the second thing she noticed.

At dinner, Sera deliberately sat closer to him than necessary.

Their shoulders touched.

Rhen glanced sideways.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Your seat is over there.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I know.”

She took another sip of tea.

[[speaker:sera]]“I'm comfortable here.”

Rhen said nothing.

Sera hid a smile behind her cup.

That night they went onto the roof.

The moon should have been visible.

Instead there was only darkness.

Then Sera saw something impossible.

Rhen was looking at a moon that nobody else could see.

She reached for his hand.

He looked down.

She did not let go.

[[speaker:sera]]“Don't explain it yet.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I wasn't going to.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Good.”

For once, Rhen smiled first.

title: A Date Nobody Named
text:
Sera insisted they investigate the city by pretending to be ordinary travelers.

Rhen immediately understood that this was an excuse.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You could have said you wanted a day together.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I did.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You said we were investigating.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Both can be true.”

They spent the morning in the market.

Sera bought candied fruit.

Rhen bought nothing.

She stared at him until he bought a paper rabbit from a child.

[[speaker:sera]]“You are terrible at shopping.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I have very few needs.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Then I'll provide some.”

The words escaped before she could stop them.

Rhen looked at her.

Sera looked away.

[[speaker:sera]]“Don't make that face.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“What face?”

[[speaker:sera]]“That one.”

The investigation eventually led them to a closed observatory.

Inside, the walls were covered with paintings of the moon.

Every painting had been scratched out.

A scholar named Mo Yanshu finally appeared.

He was slender, dressed in dark blue, and carried no visible weapon. His eyes were calm in the way of someone who had spent years watching people lie to themselves.

[[speaker:mo]]“You are Sera.”

Sera's expression hardened.

[[speaker:sera]]“You know me?”

[[speaker:mo]]“Everyone who studies fear knows the Pale Orchid.”

He looked at Rhen.

Then paused.

[[speaker:mo]]“And you are the physician.”

Rhen nodded.

Mo smiled.

[[speaker:mo]]“Interesting.”

He did not attack.

Instead, every person in the room suddenly remembered Sera wearing a different face.

A stranger.

An enemy.

A dead woman.

Sera closed her eyes.

Her assassin training had taught her something simple: if perception became unreliable, trust pressure, breath, weight and intention.

She moved.

Her blade stopped one finger from Mo's throat.

He smiled.

[[speaker:mo]]“So the legend is real.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Which part?”

[[speaker:mo]]“The part where you refuse to let other people decide what you see.”

Rhen watched quietly.

Sera turned.

[[speaker:sera]]“And you?”

Mo's smile disappeared.

[[speaker:mo]]“I decide what people remember.”

title: World Rank #8 Arrives
text:
The city finally sent a signal.

It was not a message.

It was a broken furnace gauntlet.

Han Myeong — **World Rank #8, the Ashen Beast** — was the furnace-qi body cultivator whose endurance made prolonged fights increasingly dangerous for everyone except him.

Han Myeong, World Rank #8 — the Ashen Beast, arrived before sunset.

Sera knew him by reputation: a Marquis who had carried trapped civilians out of the Burning Valley for thirty-six hours without sleep.

Han entered the inn, saw Sera, then looked at Rhen.

He paused.

[[speaker:han]]“Physician?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“That's what people call me.”

Han frowned.

[[speaker:sera]]“Don't start.”

[[speaker:han]]“I wasn't going to.”

He was lying.

The investigation became a three-way operation: Han handled the city's missing martial masters, Sera followed the perception trail, and Rhen studied the damaged meridians.

Han eventually fought one of Mo's senior disciples.

The battle tore through an entire warehouse.

Han's furnace gauntlets glowed white-hot as he used his established Burning Wastes system.

He won.

But he was forced to admit that his opponent had never actually attacked him.

The warehouse itself had become the weapon.

Sera found the pattern.

[[speaker:sera]]“He doesn't control memories.”

Han looked over.

[[speaker:sera]]“He controls the moment before memory.”

Rhen's eyes narrowed.

That was the first time Han realized the healer had understood the technique before anyone else.

title: The Moonless Scholar
text:
Mo Yanshu finally explained the city.

Decades earlier, Yuecheng had been a center of martial astronomy. Its cultivators studied qi fluctuations through lunar cycles.

Mo had discovered a dangerous principle.

If enough people remembered the same reality, their qi gradually adapted to it.

He weaponized that phenomenon.

No spell.

No supernatural curse.

Just perception, repetition and cultivation.

The city had forgotten the moon because forgetting had become the city's collective martial habit.

Sera hated the elegance of it.

[[speaker:sera]]“You're hiding something.”

Mo smiled.

[[speaker:mo]]“Of course.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Then I'll find it.”

Rhen quietly placed a hand over Sera's wrist.

She looked at him.

He released her.

She immediately caught his hand instead.

[[speaker:sera]]“You started it.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Apparently.”

Mo watched them.

For the first time, he looked genuinely amused.

title: A Fight Without Sight
text:
Mo trapped Sera inside a false battlefield.

Every sound became wrong.

Every shadow became an enemy.

Even Rhen's voice appeared from the wrong direction.

Sera stopped listening.

She fought through pressure.

One step.

Two.

Three.

Her blade found the real man.

Mo barely escaped.

Han watched from outside.

[[speaker:han]]“She did that without qi perception.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“She learned long ago not to depend on it.”

Han looked at Rhen.

[[speaker:han]]“You know her well.”

Rhen said nothing.

Sera emerged bleeding from the shoulder.

Rhen immediately reached for her.

She caught his wrist.

[[speaker:sera]]“Later.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You're hurt.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I know.”

She smiled.

[[speaker:sera]]“You can fuss over me after I win.”

She returned to the battlefield.

Rhen's expression softened.

title: The Roof Above the Tea Shop
text:
The city rested overnight.

Sera and Rhen returned to their room.

She sat beside him.

[[speaker:sera]]“Do you ever get tired of being mysterious?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Yes.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Then stop.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I don't know how.”

She laughed.

Then, without warning, she rested her head against his shoulder.

Rhen went completely still.

[[speaker:sera]]“Don't move.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I wasn't.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Good.”

They stayed that way until dawn.

Neither mentioned it the next morning.

Both remembered.

title: The False Moon
text:
Mo activated the final formation.

The entire city began seeing a second moon.

People panicked.

Han fought three disciples simultaneously.

Sera entered the central observatory.

Rhen stayed outside.

That was deliberate.

Sera had to solve this.

She found the anchor: a mirror made from black jade.

She shattered it.

The false moon disappeared.

Mo attacked her directly.

Their fight crossed rooftops.

Sera's Pale Orchid movement turned every narrow alley into an assassination corridor.

Mo adapted.

She adapted faster.

At the final exchange, Sera disarmed him.

[[speaker:mo]]“Why are you smiling?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Because I remembered something.”

[[speaker:mo]]“What?”

[[speaker:sera]]“I'm very good at this.”

She struck.

title: The Physician's Hand
text:
Mo survived.

But his final technique began collapsing the city's meridians.

Rhen stepped forward.

He did not unveil anything new.

He simply touched the central formation.

Frozen qi spread through the structure.

The entire network stopped.

Han stared.

Sera stared longer.

[[speaker:sera]]“You could have done that yesterday.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You wanted to solve it.”

She smiled.

[[speaker:sera]]“Good answer.”

Then she kissed his cheek.

Rhen froze.

Sera walked away.

[[speaker:sera]]“That's for waiting.”

Han looked at Rhen.

Rhen looked at Han.

Han wisely said nothing.

title: The Moon Returns
text:
Sera and Han dismantled the remaining formation nodes.

Mo surrendered after realizing the city had rejected his doctrine.

At midnight, the moon appeared.

People cried.

Sera stood beside Rhen.

She slipped her fingers between his.

[[speaker:sera]]“Better.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Much.”

She leaned against him.

[[speaker:sera]]“Next time, I'm choosing the date.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Was this one a date?”

She looked at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“You really are hopeless.”

title: The Morning After
text:
They returned to the tea shop.

Sera discovered the paper rabbit Rhen had bought was still in his travel bag.

She put it on the counter.

[[speaker:sera]]“Keeping souvenirs now?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Apparently.”

She kissed his cheek again.

This time he smiled before she walked away.

The city had remembered the moon.

And Sera had decided that, perhaps, she could allow herself to remember something else.

The feeling of being wanted.

Not protected.

Wanted.
